title: Liskov Substitution Principle
description: Learn to write substitutable derived classes that preserve correctness.

data.text: The **Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)** states that objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without breaking the application.
If class B inherits from class A, you should be able to use B wherever A is expected without unexpected behavior. Violations often occur when inheritance is used incorrectly.

data.title: Violating LSP
Following LSP
Key Takeaways
points: Subclasses should be substitutable for their base classes
Avoid throwing exceptions in overridden methods
Use interfaces to define specific capabilities
data.takeaway: Design inheritance hierarchies where derived classes can safely replace base classes.
